articles.title: Government increases fines on landlords from today
articles.summary: Sir Keir Starmer’s swansong in government may be another attack on private landlords – higher fines from today. From today councils can issue fines of up to £7,000 if landlords fail to fix what the government calls “poor conditions.” Fines will apply to 21 types of hazards that are found to be serious – the […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Starting today, councils can impose fines up to £7,000 on landlords for failing to address serious property hazards, marking a significant increase in penalties.
- This move by the government, linked to Sir Keir Starmer, targets 21 specific types of hazardous conditions deemed unacceptable for rental properties.

articles.title: Nightmare for landlords trying to sell flats
articles.summary: New analysis by Zoopla shows the gap between house and flat prices across the UK is the widest it has been in 30 years – since records began.  The average price of a house is up 43% since 2016 across the UK, but flats have increased by just 10% over the same period.  As such, […]
articles.ai_summary:
- The price gap between houses and flats in the UK has reached a 30-year high, with houses up 43% since 2016 compared to just 10% for flats.  
- Landlords face significant challenges in selling flats as the disparity in property values continues to widen.

articles.title: Private renting – how has it changed since Brexit referendum?
articles.summary: As we approach the 10th anniversary of the Brexit referendum, a new analysis looks at private rental sector changes since 2016. During that time Britain’s private rented sector (PRS) has grown by an estimated 6.6% from 2.98m rental properties to 3.17m. Regional variations The overall increase in stock has been driven by England, where the […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Since the Brexit referendum in 2016, the UK's private rented sector has expanded by 6.6%, rising from 2.98 million to 3.17 million rental properties.  
- Growth in the private rental market has been predominantly driven by England, highlighting regional variations in housing availability.
